items.summary: A spinning machine driven by wind, steam, or flowing water.

items.name: Workshop
items.summary: A practical place filled with tools, benches, and half-made ideas.

items.name: Blueprint
items.summary: A precise technical drawing that guides how a structure is built.

items.name: Conveyor Belt
items.summary: A moving belt that carries goods through a production line.

items.name: 3D Printer
items.summary: A machine that builds an object layer by layer from a digital design.

items.name: Bicycle
items.summary: A human-powered two-wheeled vehicle with pedals and a chain.

items.name: Windmill
items.summary: A wind-driven mill that can grind grain or pump water.

items.name: Watermill
items.summary: A mill driven by water flowing over a turning wheel.

items.name: Piston
items.summary: A sliding component that transfers pressure into movement.

items.name: Gearbox
items.summary: A set of gears enclosed together to change speed and torque.

items.name: Kiln
items.summary: A high-temperature oven used to harden clay and other materials.

items.name: Pottery
items.summary: Bowls, plates and vessels shaped from clay and fired until hard.

items.name: Ceramic
items.summary: Clay-based material strengthened by heat into a durable solid.

items.name: Storm
items.summary: An intense spell of weather bringing strong winds, rain and changing skies.

items.name: Thunder
items.summary: A deep rumbling sound produced when lightning suddenly heats the air.

items.name: Fog
items.summary: A cloud of tiny water droplets suspended close to the ground.

items.name: Mist
items.summary: A thin veil of suspended droplets that softens distant details.

items.name: Blizzard
items.summary: A severe snowstorm with strong wind and very poor visibility.

items.name: Tornado
items.summary: A rapidly rotating column of air extending down from a storm cloud.

items.name: Hurricane
items.summary: A huge tropical cyclone fueled by warm ocean water.

items.name: Monsoon
items.summary: A seasonal wind shift that brings intense periods of rainfall.

items.name: Drizzle
items.summary: Fine and gentle rain made from very small falling droplets.

items.name: Flood
items.summary: Water covering land that is usually dry after heavy rain or overflow.

items.name: Pressure
items.summary: The force exerted over an area, important to atmospheric changes.

items.name: Humidity
items.summary: The amount of water vapor present in the surrounding air.

items.name: Forecast
items.summary: A prediction of future weather from observations and models.

items.name: Barometer
items.summary: An instrument that measures air pressure to track changing weather.

items.name: Thermometer
items.summary: A measuring instrument that reveals the temperature of a place.

items.name: Heatwave
items.summary: An extended spell of unusually hot weather across an area.

items.name: Ant
items.summary: A social insect that gathers food and works with nest mates.

items.name: Anthill
items.summary: A mound of soil built around the tunnels of an ant colony.

items.name: Beetle
items.summary: A hardy insect protected by a pair of firm wing covers.

items.name: Ladybug
items.summary: A colorful spotted beetle that often feeds on garden aphids.

items.name: Wasp
items.summary: A narrow-waisted flying insect that may hunt pests or visit flowers.

items.name: Mosquito
items.summary: A small flying insect whose females can feed on blood.

items.name: Moth
items.summary: A mostly night-flying relative of the butterfly.

items.name: Grasshopper
items.summary: A long-legged insect known for jumping across grassy fields.

items.name: Cricket
items.summary: A chirping insect that makes rhythmic sounds by rubbing its wings.

items.name: Silk
items.summary: A smooth strong natural fiber spun by certain insects.

items.name: Bee Bread
items.summary: Fermented pollen stored in honeycomb cells to nourish young bees.

items.name: Insect Hotel
items.summary: A shelter of hollow stems and timber for beneficial garden insects.

items.name: Aphid
items.summary: A tiny plant-feeding insect commonly visited by ants and ladybugs.

items.name: Termite
items.summary: A wood-eating social insect that helps break down dead plants.

items.name: Swarm
items.summary: A moving cluster of insects traveling or gathering as a group.

items.name: Praying Mantis
items.summary: A watchful insect that seizes prey with folded front legs.

items.name: Brick
items.summary: A shaped block of clay hardened by drying or firing.

items.name: Clay
items.summary: Fine mineral-rich earth that can be shaped when wet.

items.name: Cement
items.summary: A powdered binder that hardens after reacting with water.

items.name: Concrete
items.summary: A hard construction mix made from binder, water and aggregates.

items.name: Arch
items.summary: A curved structure that carries weight across an opening.

items.name: Column
items.summary: A tall load-bearing support used in buildings and monuments.

items.name: Tower
items.summary: A tall structure built for defense, observation or communication.

items.name: Cathedral
items.summary: A grand church built as a center of a bishop’s community.

items.name: Ruins
items.summary: Remains of buildings that reveal the passage of time.

items.name: Monument
items.summary: A structure preserving the memory of a person or event.

items.name: Plaza
items.summary: An open public square where streets and communities meet.

items.name: Museum
items.summary: A place that preserves and presents objects for learning.

items.name: Library
items.summary: A building that keeps books and knowledge accessible.

items.name: Canal
items.summary: A man-made waterway guiding boats or irrigation through land.

items.name: Aqueduct
items.summary: A structure that carries water across a valley or town.

items.name: Scaffold
items.summary: A temporary frame that lets builders work above the ground.

items.name: Harbor
items.summary: A sheltered coastal place where vessels can safely stop.

items.name: Compass
items.summary: An instrument that points toward magnetic north.

items.name: Navigation
items.summary: The art and science of finding a route from place to place.

items.name: Anchor
items.summary: A heavy device that holds a vessel in place against drift.

items.name: Rudder
items.summary: A steering surface that turns a boat through water.

items.name: Mast
items.summary: An upright spar that supports a sailing vessel’s sails.

items.name: Keel
items.summary: The central structural spine running along the bottom of a hull.

items.name: Sail
items.summary: A sheet of material that catches wind to move a boat.

items.name: Port
items.summary: A maritime gateway where vessels exchange goods and people.

items.name: Buoy
items.summary: A floating marker that guides boats or warns of obstacles.

items.name: Fishing Net
items.summary: A web of cord that catches fish while allowing water through.

items.name: Lifeboat
items.summary: A small boat kept ready to rescue people in danger.

items.name: Cargo Ship
items.summary: A large vessel built to carry goods across the sea.

items.name: Shipyard
items.summary: A waterfront workshop where boats are built and repaired.

items.name: Sonar
items.summary: A system that uses sound waves to detect objects underwater.

items.name: Sextant
items.summary: An optical instrument used to measure angles between stars and the horizon.

items.name: Artifact
items.summary: An object made or used by people, revealing clues about the past.

items.name: Relic
items.summary: A surviving object valued for its connection to earlier times.

items.name: Excavation
items.summary: Careful digging to uncover buried structures or objects.

items.name: Pyramid
items.summary: A monumental structure with broad base and tapering sides.

items.name: Mummy
items.summary: A body preserved by deliberate treatment or dry conditions.

items.name: Hieroglyphics
items.summary: Picture-based writing used in ancient Egyptian inscriptions.

items.name: Explorer
items.summary: A curious traveler who ventures beyond familiar places.

items.name: Expedition
items.summary: A journey organized to investigate a distant place.

items.name: Landmark
items.summary: A distinctive feature used to recognize and locate a place.

items.name: Rock Art
items.summary: Images scratched or painted onto natural stone surfaces.

items.name: Tomb
items.summary: A place built or prepared for the burial of the dead.

items.name: Archaeologist
items.summary: A specialist who studies the past through material evidence.

items.name: Treasure Map
items.summary: A drawn set of directions hinting at a hidden prize.

items.name: Ancient City
items.summary: A former urban center whose remains tell a story of civilizations.

items.name: Cave Painting
items.summary: Ancient images preserved on the stone walls of a cave.

items.name: Sarcophagus
items.summary: A decorated stone coffin used for an important burial.

items.name: Stalactite
items.summary: A mineral icicle growing down from a cave roof as dripping water leaves deposits.

items.name: Stalagmite
items.summary: A cone of stone growing upward where mineral-rich drops reach a cave floor.

items.name: Geode
items.summary: A hollow rock lined with crystals formed from mineral-rich solutions.

items.name: Obsidian
items.summary: A dark volcanic glass formed when molten rock cools very quickly.

items.name: Basalt
items.summary: A dark volcanic rock that forms when lava cools and solidifies.

items.name: Granite
items.summary: A hard speckled rock formed by the slow cooling of magma underground.

items.name: Limestone
items.summary: A sedimentary rock frequently built from ancient seashells and marine remains.

items.name: Marble
items.summary: A patterned stone produced when limestone is transformed by heat and pressure.

items.name: Erosion
items.summary: The gradual wearing away of land by moving water, wind and weather.

items.name: Sediment
items.summary: Small particles of rock and soil carried and deposited by water or wind.

items.name: Amber
items.summary: Golden fossilized tree resin that can preserve insects for millions of years.

items.name: Quartzite
items.summary: Tough metamorphic rock made when quartz-rich sandstone is heated and compressed.

items.name: Pumice
items.summary: A lightweight volcanic rock filled with bubbles from trapped volcanic gas.

items.name: Magma Chamber
items.summary: An underground reservoir of molten rock that can feed an active volcano.

items.name: Fault Line
items.summary: A fracture through the Earth where masses of rock may move past each other.

items.name: Rock Cycle
items.summary: The continuous transformation of rocks through melting, erosion and pressure.

items.name: Mangrove
items.summary: A salt-tolerant coastal tree with arching roots that shelter fish and shorelines.

items.name: Otter
items.summary: A playful semi-aquatic mammal that hunts fish in streams and coastal waters.

items.name: Heron
items.summary: A tall wading bird that waits patiently for fish in shallow water.

items.name: Tadpole
items.summary: A young amphibian with a tail that transforms as it grows into a frog.

items.name: Newt
items.summary: A small amphibian that spends part of its life in ponds and damp habitats.

items.name: Marsh
items.summary: A shallow wetland where grasses and reeds dominate the landscape.

items.name: Bog
items.summary: An acidic waterlogged habitat that slowly accumulates peat and moss.

items.name: Lagoon
items.summary: A shallow body of coastal water sheltered from the open sea.

items.name: Clam
items.summary: A two-shelled mollusc that burrows in sand and filters water for food.

items.name: Mussel
items.summary: A dark-shelled mollusc that anchors itself to rocks and filters seawater.

items.name: Kelp
items.summary: A large brown seaweed that forms underwater forests in cool coastal water.

items.name: Reef
items.summary: A shallow underwater ridge that provides habitat for a wealth of marine life.

items.name: Coral
items.summary: A colony of tiny marine animals that can build remarkable limestone structures.

items.name: Lily Pad
items.summary: A floating circular leaf that helps an aquatic lily reach sunlight.

items.name: Reed
items.summary: A tall flexible wetland plant that bends with the wind beside waterways.

items.name: Salt Marsh
items.summary: A coastal wetland where salt-tolerant plants flourish in tidal water.

items.name: Yeast
items.summary: A microscopic fungus that makes dough rise by fermenting sugars.

items.name: Croissant
items.summary: A buttery layered pastry that bakes into a golden crescent.

items.name: Bagel
items.summary: A ring-shaped bread traditionally boiled before being baked.

items.name: Pretzel
items.summary: A baked twisted bread with a distinctive looped shape and golden crust.

items.name: Pancake
items.summary: A soft round breakfast cake cooked in a pan from a pourable batter.

items.name: Waffle
items.summary: A crisp patterned breakfast cake cooked between two hot patterned plates.

items.name: Cinnamon
items.summary: A fragrant spice from the dried inner bark of certain evergreen trees.

items.name: Vanilla
items.summary: A sweet aromatic flavor made from the cured pods of a tropical orchid.

items.name: Cake
items.summary: A sweet baked dessert often layered with icing for special occasions.

items.name: Caramel
items.summary: Golden cooked sugar that adds a rich toasted sweetness to desserts.

items.name: Popcorn
items.summary: Light puffed kernels that pop when moisture inside them turns to steam.

items.name: Rice
items.summary: Small edible grains grown on a grass that thrives in flooded fields.

items.name: Noodles
items.summary: Long strands of dough cooked in water and enjoyed in countless cuisines.

items.name: Dumpling
items.summary: A small pocket of dough filled or folded then steamed, boiled or fried.

items.name: Syrup
items.summary: A thick sweet liquid made by dissolving sugar or reducing plant juices.

items.name: Pie
items.summary: A baked dish with a pastry crust around a sweet or savory filling.

items.name: Lens
items.summary: A shaped transparent piece that bends light to form or magnify images.

items.name: Prism
items.summary: A transparent solid that refracts light and separates it into colors.

items.name: Optics
items.summary: The scientific study of light, vision, reflections and image formation.

items.name: Film
items.summary: A light-sensitive sheet used to capture photographs or moving pictures.

items.name: Photograph
items.summary: A captured still image that can preserve a moment of the world.

items.name: Negative
items.summary: A photographic image in which bright and dark tones are inverted.

items.name: Darkroom
items.summary: A light-controlled room where photographic film and prints are developed.

items.name: Flash
items.summary: A brief brilliant burst of light used to illuminate a camera scene.

items.name: Tripod
items.summary: A stable three-legged stand that keeps cameras steady during exposure.

items.name: Shutter
items.summary: A camera mechanism controlling how long light reaches the image sensor.

items.name: Projector
items.summary: A device that casts enlarged images onto a distant screen.

items.name: Slide
items.summary: A transparent photograph or image intended for projection onto a screen.

items.name: Photographer
items.summary: A person who creates pictures by choosing light, framing and timing.

items.name: Exposure
items.summary: The amount of light reaching a photographic surface over time.

items.name: Portrait
items.summary: An image that focuses on the likeness and expression of a person.

items.name: Aperture
items.summary: An adjustable opening in a lens that controls how much light enters.
